title: The Nordic Model Under Deglobalization
gist: This is only a short teaser/abstract for a paywalled Gavekal report: it frames the question of whether Sweden and its Nordic peers (Finland, Denmark) can sustain their post-2022 recovery given deglobalization, trade wars and Chinese competition threaten their German-style export-surplus growth model, noting four-year growth has been weak (about 1% in Sweden, stagnant in Finland, and Denmark's growth propped up by a single pharmaceutical company).

themes.theme: Nordic export model's exposure to deglobalization

insights.claim: The Nordic economies, excluding oil-rich Norway, built their prosperity on selling a diversified range of products to the world, combining persistent current account surpluses with fiscal restraint at home, a model similar to Germany's.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Investors should treat Sweden, Finland and Denmark as a bloc structurally analogous to Germany, so signals of German industrial malaise (weak exports, trade friction) are a useful leading indicator for these smaller open economies.
insights.locator: The shared weakness looks troubling given that all three economies are built on a similar model

insights.claim: Because the Nordic model depends on selling diversified exports globally, growing geopolitical fragmentation, trade wars and rising Chinese competition should leave Sweden, Finland and Denmark unusually exposed economically.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Watch Nordic export volumes and China-related trade competition (e.g. a Europe-centered 'China shock') as an early-warning proxy for stress in these export-dependent economies.
insights.locator: Geopolitical fragmentation, trade wars and Chinese competition should therefore leave them unusually exposed

insights.claim: The Nordic economies' recent growth weakness could be read as another expression of Germany's broader industrial malaise, though the author frames this as an open question rather than a settled conclusion.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: If confirmed, this framing would extend the 'German industrial malaise' investment narrative to Nordic equities and currencies, widening the set of markets exposed to the same deglobalization trade.
insights.quote: the Nordics might seem another expression of Germany’s industrial malaise
insights.locator: with four-year growth averaging just 1% in Sweden

insights.claim: Following the struggles that began in 2022, Sweden's economy is now recovering, with domestic demand rebounding and manufacturing proving surprisingly resilient.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A resilient Swedish manufacturing sector alongside recovering domestic demand is a tentative bullish signal for Swedish domestic-facing assets, contingent on whether deglobalization risks derail the export side.
insights.locator: As Sweden moves on from its recent election

insights.claim: Over the trailing four years, Sweden's economy has grown at an average rate of just 1%, Finland's economy has stagnated, and Denmark's headline growth has been flattered by the boom of a single pharmaceutical company rather than broad-based strength.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Denmark's GDP figures should be discounted for concentration risk in one pharma name, while Sweden and Finland's weak multi-year growth trends warrant closer scrutiny of underlying drivers before betting on a durable recovery.
insights.quote: four-year growth averaging just 1% in Sweden, stagnating in Finland and flattered by a single pharmaceutical company’s boom in Denmark
insights.locator: with four-year growth averaging just 1% in Sweden
